Subject: Tailored dedicated capacity recap & operational next steps

Hi Rajesh / Priya —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our side to make sure we captured everything correctly and to call out the concrete next steps: 

Key pain points you reiterated
- Periodic latency spikes during batch scoring (~p95 spikes to 400–600ms on inference paths) when traffic funnels into your real-time API.
- Strong isolation requirement for PHI inference routing (must be dedicated hardware, no co-tenancy with other customers).
- Predictable monthly cost needs for Q1 pilot; procurement needs a clear committed GPU count and SLOs.

Goals we heard
- Stable p95 latency target of <= 150ms for typical inference payloads (32–64 tokens) under sustained load.
- Dedicated pool for production traffic with burst capacity for onboarding and experiments.
- SOC2 evidence and audit logs for the pilot.

Initial sizing & architecture suggestion (ballpark)
- Reserved pool: 6–8 HGX/A100-equivalent GPUs to meet baseline throughput for the 2k rps peak window you described.
- Isolation: tenant-dedicated nodes + VPC peering to meet PHI controls (we can offer HSM/KMS integration for keying).
- Burst model: automatic burst to a shared overflow pool up to 2x for short windows (billing separate, configurable cap).

Proposed SLA anchors
- Uptime: 99.9% for the dedicated pool (monthly), with an operational runbook and automatic fallback to a compatible smaller model if infra issues occur.
- Latency: target p95 <= 150ms; we can include a p99 escalation clause in the contract where applicable.

Attachments: attached a draft MOP and a short SLA table showing tradeoffs between dedicated sizes (novex-mop-draft.pdf, sla-diff-table.xlsx).

Immediate next steps we propose
1) Technical deep-dive (90m) with your infra team + our runtime engineers — propose Fri 20 Nov, 10:00–11:30 PST.
2) Provide a formal capacity quote and a procurement-ready one-pager for your Sourcing team (we’ll circulate by EOD Thu).
3) Exchange SOC2 evidence and start a short questionnaire for compliance items — Marissa will own evidence collation.
4) Internal legal/procurement kickoff — Ben will follow up on discount thresholds and contract cadence.

If that aligns, I’ll schedule the deep-dive and drop updated artifacts into the HubSpot record and a shared Drive link.

Thanks,

Monica Patel

Rajesh / Priya —

Perfect — thanks for the quick confirmation and for the questions. Short updates ahead of the deep-dive: 

1) Canary & rollout: we will share a 6-step canary playbook in the Friday call. Highlights: staged traffic ramp (0% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%), health thresholds (error rate >1% or p99 increase >2x triggers rollback), and a 2-hour observation window before declaring full cutover.

2) Cold-start behavior: warm cache preloading reduces first-token latency; for long-tail models we recommend a background warmup job 30–60 minutes before major traffic bursts. We’ll include exact numbers per-model in the deep-dive artifacts.

3) Data residency: we’ll restrict the pilot to our us-west-2 region and VPC peering with your VPC will satisfy the residency and network isolation requirement. KMS integration supported.
